answer: Sybil resistance begins with hardware attestation: every agent must present a signed quote from a secure enclave whose key was provisioned once, so a thousand sock-puppet identities would cost a thousand real chips. When an operator expands, the enclave pins each new node to the same root and publishes an echo of that binding, a verifiable bridge letting peers confirm lineage without trusting a central registry. Stake then flows through a bonded vault, slashed on any duplicate attestation, making duplication expensive instead of free.
